23/**
24 * Encapsulates functionality and implementation that is common to all families
25 * of one-dimensional barcodes.
26 *
27 * @author dswitkin@google.com (Daniel Switkin)
28 * @author Sean Owen
29 */
30pub trait OneDReader: Reader {
31    const QUIET_ZONE: usize = 15;
32    /**
33     * We're going to examine rows from the middle outward, searching alternately above and below the
34     * middle, and farther out each time. rowStep is the number of rows between each successive
35     * attempt above and below the middle. So we'd scan row middle, then middle - rowStep, then
36     * middle + rowStep, then middle - (2 * rowStep), etc.
37     * rowStep is bigger as the image is taller, but is always at least 1. We've somewhat arbitrarily
38     * decided that moving up and down by about 1/16 of the image is pretty good; we try more of the
39     * image if "trying harder".
40     *
41     * @param image The image to decode
42     * @param hints Any hints that were requested
43     * @return The contents of the decoded barcode
44     * @throws NotFoundException Any spontaneous errors which occur
45     */
46    fn _do_decode<B: Binarizer>(
47        &mut self,
48        image: &mut BinaryBitmap<B>,
49        hints: &DecodeHints,
50    ) -> Result<RXingResult> {
51        let mut hints = hints.clone();
52        let width = image.get_width();
53        let height = image.get_height();
54
55        let try_harder = hints.TryHarder.unwrap_or(false);
56
57        let try_pure = hints.PureBarcode.unwrap_or(false);
58
59        // Attempt to decode the barcode as "pure". This method may be very inneficient and uses
60        // a very poor version of a binarizer.
61        // ToDo: Add a better binarizer for pure barcodes
62        if try_pure {
63            let mid_line = 1.max(image.get_height() / 2);
64
65            let rw = image
66                .get_source()
67                .get_row(mid_line)
68                .ok_or(Exceptions::index_out_of_bounds_with("row out of bounds"))?;
69
70            let decoded = self.decode_pure(mid_line as u32, &rw, &hints);
71            if decoded.is_ok() {
72                return decoded;
73            }
74        }
75
76        let row_step = usize::max(1, height >> (if try_harder { 8 } else { 5 }));
77        let max_lines = if try_harder {
78            height // Look at the whole image, not just the center
79        } else {
80            15 // 15 rows spaced 1/32 apart is roughly the middle half of the image
81        };
82
83        let middle = height / 2;
84        for x in 0..max_lines {
85            // Scanning from the middle out. Determine which row we're looking at next:
86            let row_steps_above_or_below = x.div_ceil(2);
87            let is_above = (x & 0x01) == 0; // i.e. is x even?
88            let row_number: isize = middle as isize
89                + row_step as isize
90                    * (if is_above {
91                        row_steps_above_or_below as isize
92                    } else {
93                        -(row_steps_above_or_below as isize)
94                    });
95            if row_number < 0 || row_number >= height as isize {
96                // Oops, if we run off the top or bottom, stop
97                break;
98            }
99
100            // Estimate black point for this row and load it:
101            let mut row = if let Ok(res) = image.get_black_row(row_number as usize) {
102                res
103            } else {
104                continue;
105            };
106
107            // While we have the image data in a BitArray, it's fairly cheap to reverse it in place to
108            // handle decoding upside down barcodes.
109            for attempt in 0..2 {
110                // for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) {
111                if attempt == 1 {
112                    // trying again?
113
114                    // reverse the row and continue
115                    // This means we will only ever draw result points *once* in the life of this method
116                    // since we want to avoid drawing the wrong points after flipping the row, and,
117                    // don't want to clutter with noise from every single row scan -- just the scans
118                    // that start on the center line.
119                    row.to_mut().reverse();
120
121                    hints.NeedResultPointCallback = None;
122                }
123                let Ok(mut result) = self.decode_row(row_number as u32, &row, &hints) else {
124                    continue;
125                };
126                // We found our barcode
127                if attempt == 1 {
128                    // But it was upside down, so note that
129                    result.putMetadata(
130                        RXingResultMetadataType::ORIENTATION,
131                        RXingResultMetadataValue::Orientation(180),
132                    );
133                    // And remember to flip the result points horizontally.
134                    let points = result.getPointsMut();
135                    if !points.is_empty() && points.len() >= 2 {
136                        points[0] = point(width as f32 - points[0].x - 1.0, points[0].y);
137                        points[1] = point(width as f32 - points[1].x - 1.0, points[1].y);
138                    }
139                }
140                return Ok(result);
141            }
142        }
143
144        Err(Exceptions::NOT_FOUND)
145    }
146
147    /**
148     * <p>Attempts to decode a one-dimensional barcode format given a single row of
149     * an image.</p>
150     *
151     * @param rowNumber row number from top of the row
152     * @param row the black/white pixel data of the row
153     * @param hints decode hints
154     * @return {@link RXingResult} containing encoded string and start/end of barcode
155     * @throws NotFoundException if no potential barcode is found
156     * @throws ChecksumException if a potential barcode is found but does not pass its checksum
157     * @throws FormatException if a potential barcode is found but format is invalid
158     */
159    fn decode_row(
160        &mut self,
161        rowNumber: u32,
162        row: &BitArray,
163        hints: &DecodeHints,
164    ) -> Result<RXingResult>;
165
166    fn decode_pure(
167        &mut self,
168        rowNumber: u32,
169        row: &[u8],
170        hints: &DecodeHints,
171    ) -> Result<RXingResult> {
172        if row.is_empty() {
173            return Err(Exceptions::NOT_FOUND);
174        }
175
176        let new_row = pad_bitarray(row, Self::QUIET_ZONE);
177
178        self.decode_row(rowNumber, &new_row, hints)
179    }
180}
181
182// Add a buffer on either side of the row to mimic a quiet zone. This may not exist in a "pure barcode"
183fn pad_bitarray(bits: &[u8], quiet_zone: usize) -> BitArray {
184    const PIXEL_COLOR_SPLIT_POINT: u8 = u8::MAX / 2;
185
186    let mut new_row = BitArray::with_capacity(bits.len() + (quiet_zone * 2));
187
188    let value = bits[0] >= PIXEL_COLOR_SPLIT_POINT;
189
190    for _ in 0..quiet_zone {
191        new_row.appendBit(value);
192    }
193
194    for bit in bits {
195        new_row.appendBit(bit < &PIXEL_COLOR_SPLIT_POINT)
196    }
197
198    for _ in 0..quiet_zone {
199        new_row.appendBit(value);
200    }
201
202    new_row
203}

205/**
206 * Determines how closely a set of observed counts of runs of black/white values matches a given
207 * target pattern. This is reported as the ratio of the total variance from the expected pattern
208 * proportions across all pattern elements, to the length of the pattern.
209 *
210 * @param counters observed counters
211 * @param pattern expected pattern
212 * @param maxIndividualVariance The most any counter can differ before we give up
213 * @return ratio of total variance between counters and pattern compared to total pattern size
214 */
215pub fn pattern_match_variance(
216    counters: &[u32],
217    pattern: &[u32],
218    mut max_individual_variance: f32,
219) -> f32 {
220    let num_counters = counters.len();
221
222    let total: f32 = counters.iter().sum::<u32>() as f32;
223    let pattern_length: u32 = pattern.iter().take(num_counters).sum();
224    if total < pattern_length as f32 {
225        // If we don't even have one pixel per unit of bar width, assume this is too small
226        // to reliably match, so fail:
227        return f32::INFINITY;
228    }
229
230    let unit_bar_width = total / pattern_length as f32;
231    max_individual_variance *= unit_bar_width;
232
233    let mut total_variance = 0.0;
234    for (&counter, scaled_pattern) in counters.iter().zip(
235        pattern
236            .iter()
237            .take(num_counters)
238            .map(|&p| (p as f32) * unit_bar_width),
239    ) {
240        // for x in 0..num_counters {
241        // let counter = counters[x];
242        // let scaled_pattern = (pattern as f32) * unit_bar_width;
243        let variance = if (counter as f32) > scaled_pattern {
244            counter as f32 - scaled_pattern
245        } else {
246            scaled_pattern - counter as f32
247        };
248        if variance > max_individual_variance {
249            return f32::INFINITY;
250        }
251        total_variance += variance;
252    }
253    total_variance / total
254}

256/**
257 * Records the size of successive runs of white and black pixels in a row, starting at a given point.
258 * The values are recorded in the given array, and the number of runs recorded is equal to the size
259 * of the array. If the row starts on a white pixel at the given start point, then the first count
260 * recorded is the run of white pixels starting from that point; likewise it is the count of a run
261 * of black pixels if the row begin on a black pixels at that point.
262 *
263 * @param row row to count from
264 * @param start offset into row to start at
265 * @param counters array into which to record counts
266 * @throws NotFoundException if counters cannot be filled entirely from row before running out
267 *  of pixels
268 */
269pub fn record_pattern(row: &BitArray, start: usize, counters: &mut [u32]) -> Result<()> {
270    let num_counters = counters.len();
271    counters.fill(0);
272
273    let end = row.get_size();
274    if start >= end {
275        return Err(Exceptions::NOT_FOUND);
276    }
277
278    let mut is_white = !row.get(start);
279    let mut counter_position = 0;
280    let mut i = start;
281    while i < end {
282        if row.get(i) != is_white {
283            counters[counter_position] += 1;
284        } else {
285            counter_position += 1;
286            if counter_position == num_counters {
287                break;
288            } else {
289                counters[counter_position] = 1;
290                is_white = !is_white;
291            }
292        }
293        i += 1;
294    }
295    // If we read fully the last section of pixels and filled up our counters -- or filled
296    // the last counter but ran off the side of the image, OK. Otherwise, a problem.
297    if !(counter_position == num_counters || (counter_position == num_counters - 1 && i == end)) {
298        return Err(Exceptions::NOT_FOUND);
299    }
300    Ok(())
301}
302
303pub fn record_pattern_in_reverse(row: &BitArray, start: usize, counters: &mut [u32]) -> Result<()> {
304    let mut start = start;
305    // This could be more efficient I guess
306    let mut num_transitions_left = counters.len() as isize;
307    let mut last = row.get(start);
308    while start > 0 && num_transitions_left >= 0 {
309        start -= 1;
310        if row.get(start) != last {
311            num_transitions_left -= 1;
312            last = !last;
313        }
314    }
315    if num_transitions_left >= 0 {
316        return Err(Exceptions::NOT_FOUND);
317    }
318    record_pattern(row, start + 1, counters)?;
319
320    Ok(())
321}
